state.misconception_label: Believes f(x - a) translates the function up a units

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The correct transformation for \( y = f(x - 3) \) is a translation to the right by 3 units, not up. Remember, when dealing with functions, shifting inside the parentheses affects the horizontal direction, not the vertical. Keep this in mind when determining translations in the future.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so it's to the right, not up! But I'm still a bit confused about why it goes right when there's a minus sign inside the brackets - like, shouldn't minus mean it goes left or something? Can you explain that bit?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Absolutely! I understand why that might be confusing. When we have a minus sign inside the brackets, like in \( y = f(x - 3) \), it actually shifts the graph to the right by 3 units. Think of it as the opposite of what you might expect - it's a common misconception. Just remember, when dealing with functions, the sign inside the parentheses affects the horizontal direction, not the vertical.
